This page is the interactive version of the lesson notes (PDF). Each section
starts with a question about a game. Then it explains the idea behind it. It
ends with a **Do it** task and one set of questions. The full explanations,
examples and exercises are in the notes.

## Key terms

{{< glossary linear-narrative branching-narrative branch-and-bottleneck player-agency environmental-storytelling narrative-structure story-beat player-experience >}}

## 5.1 One road through the story: linear narrative

- In a **linear narrative**, every player meets the same events in the same
  order and sees the same ending.
- The player decides **how** to play a stage, not **what** happens in the
  story.
- Strengths: the writer controls the tension curve and the climax; each
  scene is written once, so it costs less.
- Weakness: the player cannot change the story.
- *Moon Diver* (lecture 4) is linear: eight stages, always in the same
  order, one ending.

![A linear narrative: one road.](images/linear.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Linear is not the same as boring. It describes the structure, not the
quality.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Linear or not?"}
Choose a game with a story. Write two choices that you made. Did each one
change the story (what happens) or only the gameplay (how you play)? Is the
narrative linear?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Linear"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="it has many endings"}
Every player sees the same stages in the same order and the same ending. What kind of narrative is it?
:   linear

In a linear game, what does the player decide?
:   how to play a stage

A player chooses a weapon, but the story is always the same. What does the choice change?
:   only the gameplay

Name one strength of a linear story.
:   the writer controls the tension

Name one weakness of a linear story.
:   the player cannot change the story
:::
:::

## 5.2 Choices that change the story: branching narrative

- In a **branching narrative**, the player's choices lead to different
  scenes and endings.
- When choices really matter, the player feels **agency**.
- The cost: every choice opens new scenes. 2 options, 3 decisions in a
  full tree: **15 scenes, 8 endings**, and one player sees only 4.
- **Branch and bottleneck:** the paths join again at key scenes. The same 3
  choices: **9 scenes, 2 endings**.
- *Silent Station*: footprints or radio → both meet at the antenna (the
  bottleneck) → two endings. 6 scenes in all.

![A full tree and branch and bottleneck.](images/branching.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
A fake choice changes nothing. At a bottleneck, the earlier choice should
still leave a mark: a line, an object, a character who remembers.
:::

{{< sim file="sims/branch-builder.html" poster="sims/branch-builder.png" title="Branch Builder: how many scenes must the writers make?" height="640" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Branch Builder"}
In **Branch Builder**, set 2 choices and 3 decisions. Write the scenes and
the endings for a full tree, then for branch and bottleneck. Do it again
with 3 choices. Why do writers let paths join?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Branches"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="16|3"}
A full tree: 3 decisions with 2 options each. How many endings?
:   8

A full tree: 2 decisions with 2 options each. How many endings?
:   4

The paths join again at key scenes. What is this structure called?
:   branch and bottleneck

The player feels that choices really matter. What is it called?
:   player agency

Why do writers let paths join again?
:   to write far fewer scenes
:::
:::

## 5.3 The world tells the story: environmental storytelling

- **Environmental storytelling:** places and objects tell the story. The
  player discovers it by exploring.
- Tools: objects, notes, damage, light, sound, the place of things.
- Strengths: the player finds the story like a detective; it does not stop
  the gameplay (no long cutscene); it works with linear and branching
  stories.
- The station room: a cup of cold tea (someone left in a hurry), a burnt
  radio (no call for help), "supply truck" circled (the truck did not
  come), a note and footprints (Aziz went to the antenna).

![The empty room of Silent Station.](images/station-room.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
A plant or a chair is decoration, not a clue. A clue must point to an event
of the story.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Find the clues"}
Choose one place in a game that you know (or the room above). List three
objects or details. For each one, write what it tells about the story.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Read the room"}
The room of Silent Station. Choose what each object tells.

::: {.match extra="Mira is hungry"}
A full cup of cold tea.
:   someone left in a hurry

A burnt radio.
:   nobody could call for help

"Supply truck" is circled on yesterday's date.
:   the truck did not come

Footprints lead out of the door towards the hill.
:   someone walked to the antenna

How does the player get this story?
:   by exploring the room
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Silent Station {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

*Silent Station* is a mobile game. Mira, a radio operator, arrives at an
empty research station in the desert. The room tells what happened: a cup
of cold tea, a note from Aziz ("Gone to fix the antenna. Back by 6."), a
burnt radio, a circled day ("supply truck") and footprints to the door.
Then Mira chooses: **follow the footprints** or **repair the radio first**.
Both paths lead to the **antenna on the hill**, where Aziz sits with a hurt
foot. There she chooses again: **help Aziz fix the antenna** (ending A) or
**take Aziz back to the station first** (ending B).

{{< sim file="sims/silent-station.html" poster="sims/silent-station.png" title="Silent Station: explore the room, then choose" kind="game" height="780" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · The structure of Silent Station"}
Silent Station: the room, then footprints or radio, then the antenna, then
ending A or ending B. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="4|ending A"}
Which part is environmental storytelling?
:   the room with its objects

Which scene is the bottleneck?
:   the antenna on the hill

How many endings does the game have?
:   2

How many scenes are there in all (arrival, two first choices, the antenna, two endings)?
:   6
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · Change the design (harder)"}
Silent Station as above. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="12|branching"}
The two first paths do not join; each one has its own antenna scene with two endings. How many endings now?
:   4

With the same change, how many scenes in all?
:   9

The designer removes both choices. What kind of narrative is left?
:   linear, with environmental storytelling

Both first paths reach the antenna, and nothing there is different. What is the risk?
:   a fake choice

What could show that Mira repaired the radio first?
:   the radio hums in the background
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- Linear: one road, the same events and ending for every player.
- Branching: choices lead to different scenes and endings and give agency.
- A full tree grows fast; branch and bottleneck joins paths at key scenes.
- Environmental storytelling: places and objects tell the story.
- Many games mix the three ways.
